source_text: CAPUT SECUNDUM, De ortu hominis specialiter, ubi nominatim de DEI exsistentia. Ortus hominis habet principium & modum. Non de principio temporis, in quo homo esse coepit, & est sextus dies mundi creationis, hic agimus: sed de principio productionis, a quo est & regitur.
english: CHAPTER TWO. On the origin of man specially, where namely of the existence of GOD.

The origin of man has a principle and a mode. We are not treating here of the principle of time in which man began to be, which is the sixth day of the world's creation, but of the principle of production, from which he is and by which he is ruled.

source_text: I. Principium hominis est Deus. Nam a Deo homo conditus est Gen. 1.26-27. Quoniam vero homo a Deo est, & ab eo secundum considerationem Theologicam proxime dependet, hic locus proprius est, ubi de Deo agatur. Jam vero hominem ad Deum, regem & principium suum reducere & ad vitam aeternam deducere non potest Theologus, nisi DEUM cognitum habeat. Hinc & Apostolus Act. 17.24-31 Deum creatorem praedicat; nunc mandat omnibus ut resipiscant, eo quod statuit diem judicii per Christum a mortuis suscitatum.
english: I. The principle of man is God. For man was created by God (Genesis 1:26-27).

But since man is from God and depends on Him most nearly according to theological consideration, this is the proper place to treat of God. For the theologian cannot lead man back to God his King and principle, and onward to eternal life, unless he has God known.
Hence the Apostle too (Acts 17:24-31) proclaims God the creator; and now commands all everywhere to repent, because He has appointed a day of judgment through Christ raised from the dead.

source_text: II. Deus vero, ut in se est, a nemine, nisi a seipso cognosci potest, 1 Tim. 6.16; ut autem sese nobis revelavit, videtur quasi a tergo, Exod. 33.23, non clare, sed aenigmatice, 1 Cor. 13.12. Quod vero revelatum est de Deo, id sufficit nobis ad bene vivendum, Deut. 29.29. III. Hoc autem quod sciri potest de Deo, est ejus sufficientia & efficientia. Haec duo sunt columnae fidei. IV. Sufficientia Dei est, qua ipse in se se sibi nobisque satis habet: omnipotens, nullius indigus & indefectus. V. Sufficientia Dei spectatur in ejus exsistentia, essentia & subsistentia.
english: II. But God, as He is in Himself, can be known by no one except by Himself (1 Timothy 6:16); yet as He has revealed Himself to us, He is seen as it were from behind (Exodus 33:23), not clearly but enigmatically (1 Corinthians 13:12). But what has been revealed about God suffices for us to live well (Deuteronomy 29:29).
III. Now this which can be known of God is His sufficiency and efficiency. These two are the pillars of faith.

IV. God's sufficiency is that by which He in Himself has enough for Himself and for us: almighty, needing no one and without defect. V. God's sufficiency is considered in His existence, essence, and subsistence.

source_text: VI. Deus est, hoc est, actu exsistit. PRIMUM ac summum omnis verae religionis fundamentum & axioma est, Deum esse, juxta illud Heb. 11.6: Qui accedit ad Deum, hunc credere oportet, esse Deum. Deum vero esse est quidem per se notum secundum naturam; non tamen secundum nos, quorum notitia a sensibus incipit, ideoque non, nisi praevio aliquo discursu, huic propositioni assentimur, Rom. 1.20; Act. 17.28; Sap. 13. Cum autem de Deo loquimur, communi animorum conceptione intelligimus ens perfectissimum, primum, potentissimum, sapientissimum, optimum, omnium causam producentem & gubernantem omnia.
english: VI. God is, that is, He actually exists. The first and highest foundation and axiom of all true religion is that God is, according to Hebrews 11:6: whoever comes to God must believe that God is.

That God is is indeed known in itself according to nature; yet not according to us, whose knowledge begins from the senses, and therefore we assent only by some prior discourse (Romans 1:20; Acts 17:28; Wisdom 13).
When we speak of God, by the common conception of minds we understand the most perfect being, the first, most powerful, most wise, and best, the producing cause of all things and the governor of all.

source_text: Demonstrari tamen potest ex sensibus contra eos qui negant Deum esse, ut Diagoras & Epicurus. Quamquam omni creaturae rationali notum sit Deum esse, & pii omnes Scriptura tum interno Spiritus S. testimonio persuasi sint: tamen propter Atheorum hujus aevi impudentiam rationibus breviter non a priori sed a posteriori, h. e. effectis demonstrandum est, tum axiomatis theoreticis, tum publica naturae voce, tum perpetuo omnium nationum consensu, tum axiomate practico quod cuivis conscientia dictat.
english: Yet it can be demonstrated from the senses against those who deny that God is, such as Diagoras and Epicurus.

Although it is known to every rational creature that God is, and all the pious are persuaded by Scripture and the inward testimony of the Holy Spirit: yet because of the impudence of this age's atheists it must briefly be demonstrated not a priori but a posteriori from effects — by theoretical axioms, by nature's public voice, by the perpetual consensus of all nations, and by the practical axiom which conscience dictates.

source_text: RATIO PRIMA fundatur in axiomate a rerum singulari exsistentia & coordinatione. Nihil eorum quae sensu percipimus est a seipso. Ergo unum ens necessario praeexsistit a quo ut causa prima omnia ortum ducunt. At hoc ens primum est Deus. RATIO SECUNDA fundatur in axiomate a sapientia prima. Omnis causa efficiens primaria suo effectu praestantior est. Ergo una suprema & sapientissima mens. At haec Deus est. RATIO QUARTA fundatur in axiomate ab amore primo. Omnia amant se esse. Hic amor non est per se sed participatus. Ergo datur primus amor per se. At hic Deus est.
english: THE FIRST REASON is founded on the axiom from things' singular existence and coordination. Nothing we perceive by sense is from itself. Therefore some one being necessarily pre-exists from which as first cause all draw origin. But this first being is God.
THE SECOND REASON is founded on the axiom from first wisdom. Every primary efficient cause is more excellent than its effect. Therefore there is one supreme and most wise mind. But this is God.
THE FOURTH REASON is founded on the axiom from first love. All things love to be. This love is not through itself but participated. Therefore there is a first love through itself. But this is God.

source_text: RATIO QUINTA fundatur in axiomate ab exsistentia universi. Mundus non fuit semper, quia e partibus constat. Ergo e nihilo productus est. At hic est Deus. RATIO SEXTA fundatur in publica naturae voce. Magnitudo, multitudo, varietas, pulchritudo, perfectio clamant ab aliquo uno esse omnia. At hic est Deus. RATIO SEPTIMA fundatur in rerum ordine & dispositione ad finem, etiam earum quae rationis expertes sunt. Omnis ordo ab uno est. At hic Deus est. RATIO OCTAVA fundatur in contrariorum indole & inimicitia; opus est moderatore. At hic Deus est.
english: THE FIFTH REASON is founded on the axiom from the universe's existence. The world was not always, because it consists of parts. Therefore it was produced from nothing. But this is God.
THE SIXTH REASON is founded on nature's public voice. Magnitude, multitude, variety, beauty, and perfection cry out that all are from some one. But this is God.
THE SEVENTH REASON is founded on the order of things and their disposition to an end, even of those that lack reason. Every order is from one. But this is God.
THE EIGHTH REASON is founded on the temper and enmity of contraries; a moderator is needed. But this is God.

source_text: RATIO NONA fundatur in fabrica corporis tam affabre ordinata. Non nisi a sapientissimo opifice. At hic Deus est. RATIO DECIMA fundatur in contemplatione astrorum mira arte rotantium. At hic Deus est. RATIO UNDECIMA fundatur in fatali ac necessaria harmonia rerum. At haec Deus est. RATIO DUODECIMA fundatur in artibus humanis. Si arte & sapientia regitur homo, necesse est totum mundum arte & sapientia regi. Atque ideo Deo credamus.
english: THE NINTH REASON is founded on the body's fabric so skillfully ordered. Only by a most wise craftsman. But this is God.
THE TENTH REASON is founded on contemplation of the stars revolving with marvelous art. But this is God.
THE ELEVENTH REASON is founded on the fatal and necessary harmony of things. But this is God.
THE TWELFTH REASON is founded on the human arts. If man is ruled by art and wisdom, the whole world must be ruled by art and wisdom. And therefore let us believe God.

source_text: RATIO DECIMA TERTIA fundatur in miraculis quae totam creati universi vim excedunt. Ergo causa est quae universum exsuperet. At illa est Deus. RATIO DECIMA QUARTA fundatur in societatis oeconomicae, scholasticae, politicae, ecclesiasticae conservatione, quae nisi ab uno praepotente servari non posset. At ille est Deus. RATIO DECIMA QUINTA fundatur in praedictionibus rerum futurarum & earum impletione, Esa. 41.22-23. RATIO DECIMA SEXTA fundatur in optimorum hominum autoritate: Moses, Prophetae, Apostoli, melioresque philosophi miraculis, sanctitate, martyrio, prophetia probarunt.
english: THE THIRTEENTH REASON is founded on miracles that exceed the whole force of the created universe. Therefore there is a cause that surpasses the universe. But that is God.
THE FOURTEENTH REASON is founded on the conservation of economic, scholastic, political, and ecclesiastical society, which could not be kept except by one all-powerful. But that one is God.
THE FIFTEENTH REASON is founded on predictions of future things and their fulfillment (Isaiah 41:22-23).
THE SIXTEENTH REASON is founded on the authority of the best men: Moses, the Prophets, the Apostles, and the better philosophers proved it by miracles, holiness, martyrdom, and prophecy.

source_text: RATIO DECIMA SEPTIMA fundatur in perpetuo & universali omnium nationum & legislatorum consensu. Omnes asserunt Deum esse. Qui hunc consensum negat, is etiam Romam esse & Caesarem fuisse negabit. RATIO DECIMA OCTAVA fundatur in axiomate practico quod cuivis conscientia dictat. Omnibus conscientia inest quae in benefactis exhilarat, in malefactis cruciat, Rom. 2.15; Sap. 17.11. Ex quo colligitur esse judicem supremum. At hic Deus est. Caeterum, an ex motu Deum esse concludi possit? Qui cum Aristotele ex hoc probant, gemino laborant paralogismo. Sed rationes quibus demonstravimus Deum esse impræsentiarum sufficere possunt.
english: THE SEVENTEENTH REASON is founded on the perpetual and universal consensus of all nations and lawgivers. All assert that God is. Whoever denies this consensus will also deny that Rome is and that Caesar was.

THE EIGHTEENTH REASON is founded on the practical axiom which conscience dictates. In all there is a conscience which in good deeds cheers, in evil torments (Romans 2:15; Wisdom 17:11). From which it is gathered that there is a supreme judge. But this is God.

For the rest, whether from motion it can be concluded that God is: those who with Aristotle prove from this labor under a double paralogism. But the reasons by which we have demonstrated that God is can suffice for the present.
